what_its_for: Amiloride is a 'water pill' (diuretic) that helps your kidneys remove extra fluid from your body while keeping your potassium levels from dropping too low. It is used to treat high blood pressure, fluid buildup (swelling), and low potassium levels. It is often used together with other water pills like furosemide or hydrochlorothiazide.
how_to_take: Take amiloride by mouth with food or milk to help prevent stomach upset. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Do not take it at bedtime, because it may cause you to need to urinate during the night. Take it exactly as your doctor prescribed — do not take more or less than instructed.
dosing: The usual starting dose for adults is 5 mg once daily, which may be increased to 10 mg per day if needed. Your doctor will set the right dose for you based on your condition and other medications. Never adjust your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Never double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store amiloride at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. If you no longer need the medication, ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating large amounts of high-potassium foods such as bananas, oranges, potatoes, tomatoes, and salt substitutes that contain potassium (like 'No Salt' or 'Nu-Salt'), because amiloride already raises your potassium levels and too much can be harmful. Avoid drinking alcohol, as it can lower your blood pressure too much. Avoid taking NSAIDs (like ibuprofen or naproxen) without asking your doctor, as they can reduce how well amiloride works. Do not take potassium supplements unless your doctor tells you to.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: muscle weakness, cramps, or paralysis; an irregular or slow heartbeat; numbness or tingling; extreme fatigue or confusion; difficulty breathing; signs of high potassium (hyperkalemia) such as chest pain or feeling your heart is beating abnormally; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; little or no urination; or severe dizziness or fainting.
when_it_works: Amiloride starts working within about 2 hours of taking your first dose. You may notice increased urination during the first few days. For blood pressure control, it may take several weeks of regular use to see the full benefit. Keep taking it even if you feel well — high blood pressure often has no symptoms.
special_populations: Kidney problems: Amiloride is NOT recommended if you have severe kidney disease or are already on kidney dialysis, because it can cause dangerously high potassium levels. Your doctor will check your kidney function before and during treatment. Diabetes: Use with caution, as amiloride may affect blood sugar control — monitor your blood sugar closely and report any changes to your doctor. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to the effects of this medication and should be monitored closely for high potassium levels and kidney function. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before taking amiloride if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as its safety in these situations needs to be carefully evaluated.
